title: The Missing Name
credit: Built on Robert's preview rewrite (preview-stories-e4e6722). Lines and reflections revised for a first-time player.

intro.kicker: City design showcase · five minutes before your slot
intro.text: Your team is about to present its plan for safer walking routes. The map on your opening slide is Asha's: she walked the neighbourhood for three weeks to draw it. Her name isn't on it.

cast.name: You
cast.role: lead the team; you made the slides

cast.name: Kit
cast.role: built the scale model; has waited all term to reveal it

cast.name: Asha
cast.role: walked and drew the map; doesn't love the spotlight

prompt: Five minutes. How will you put Asha's work back where it belongs?

setup.line: The opening slide fills the screen: a neighbourhood map, one route in red. No name beneath it.

setup.speaker: Kit
setup.line: Five minutes. Map first, then the big reveal. Wait till they see the model open.
setup.direction: excited, quick, rubbing his hands together; this reveal is his moment

setup.speaker: Asha
setup.line: That's my map. Three weeks of walking those streets. And it looks like we made it up in the studio.
setup.direction: quiet and controlled, hurt underneath; not angry, just stung

setup.speaker: You
setup.line: Asha, I left your name off. That's on me. Let's fix it before we go on.

setup.speaker: Asha
setup.line: I don't want a fuss. I can talk about the walks, I know those. I just don't want the whole pitch.
setup.direction: torn; relieved to be heard but shy of the stage

setup.speaker: Kit
setup.line: If Asha opens with the walks, there won't be time for the model. It's one or the other.
setup.direction: worried, honest, trying not to sound selfish

setup.speaker: Asha
setup.line: You could hold up my notebook and say it's mine. Or I'll open with the map myself. Either's okay. Really.
setup.direction: warm, sincere, meaning it; offering both

microphone.speaker: You
microphone.line: Before we show you anything we built, Asha is going to tell you where this map came from.
microphone.direction: clear, proud of her, handing over

microphone.line: You slide the microphone across. Asha hesitates, then takes it.

microphone.speaker: Asha
microphone.line: This corner looked like a shortcut. Then I walked it with a man pushing a shopping trolley, and the kerb stopped him dead.
microphone.direction: nervous at first, then finding her footing as she remembers

microphone.speaker: Asha
microphone.line: So we widened the turn. Forty-one people walked these streets with me. This map is really theirs.

microphone.speaker: Kit
microphone.line: And that's exactly why the model...
Time is called. The audience heard why the route bends. Kit's model stays shut in its box.

notebook.speaker: You
notebook.line: This is Asha's notebook. Every line on our map started here. She walked it for three weeks.
notebook.direction: firm, clear, making sure the room hears the name

notebook.line: Kit opens the model. The audience leans in.

notebook.speaker: Visitor
notebook.line: Why is that corner crossed out on the map?

notebook.speaker: Asha
notebook.line: A trolley got stuck there. On the third walk we...
Time is called mid-sentence. The model was seen and her name was said. Her reason wasn't heard.

lesson: Credit isn't only a name on a slide. It's whose voice explains the work, and the time to agree that is before the day.

microphone.title: You handed Asha the floor.
microphone.kept: Her work, in her own words. The audience heard why the map bends where it does.
microphone.cost: Kit's model reveal, the moment he'd waited all term for.
microphone.ask: How could Kit's work have been protected too?

notebook.title: You credited Asha inside the plan.
notebook.kept: The pitch as rehearsed: her name said clearly, and the model revealed.
notebook.cost: Her reasoning. You spoke for her work, and her own explanation was cut off.
notebook.ask: What would make Asha want the microphone next time?

microphone.label: Move the microphone
microphone.hint: Asha opens, in her own words.

notebook.label: Show the notebook
notebook.hint: You credit her; Kit keeps his reveal.
